Track 01: Machine Learning Foundations

Understand how models analyze training data, adjust weights, and spot patterns without explicit coding.

LESSON 01

Pattern vs. Program

Traditional rule-based algorithms vs. probabilistic neural networks. Understand deterministic if-else logic versus pattern recognition.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Students analyze how code executes instructions linearly while machine learning optimizes loss functions. Hands-on comparison between a tax calculator and an image classifier.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 02

How Models Learn

Data inputs, parameters, weights, loss functions, and optimization loops. Explore backpropagation and gradient descent conceptually.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Visual explanation of input layers, hidden layers, and activation thresholds. Explore how error rate drives parameter updates across training epochs.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 03

Data Diet & Bias

Training set curation, class imbalances, historical bias, and real-world failure cases in predictive models.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Case study examination of recruitment algorithms, facial recognition disparities, and the ethical mandate for representative datasets.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP

Track 02: Tool Lab & Prompt Engineering

Harness generative AI models effectively through precision structured prompting and critical evaluation.

LESSON 04

The 4 Pillars of Precision Prompting

Master Task, Details, Audience, and Format to eliminate vague responses and extract high-value insights.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Deconstruct weak prompts into robust multi-parameter instructions. Learn persona prompting, few-shot prompting, and negative constraints.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 05

Anatomy of Large Language Models

Tokenization, context windows, temperature settings, and probabilistic next-token generation.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Understanding why LLMs generate fluent text that may be factually incorrect. Exploring the mechanics of attention heads and transformer architecture.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 06

Hallucination Detection & Grounding

Techniques for cross-referencing AI outputs against primary sources, citations, and ground-truth literature.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Step-by-step methodology for checking mathematical, historical, and scientific statements generated by conversational agents.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP

Track 03: Responsible AI & Digital Citizenship

Navigate academic honesty, copyright, data privacy, synthetic media, and societal implications of AI.

LESSON 07

Academic Integrity & Boundaries

Using AI as a personal tutor vs. plagiarizing assignments. Understanding teacher expectations and transparent citations.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Scenario analysis covering outline creation, brainstorming, code debugging, and full ghostwriting violations with actionable checklists.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 08

Synthetic Media & Deepfakes

Identifying AI-generated imagery, voice clones, and synthetic misinformation in social media ecosystems.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Visual artifacts analysis: hands, textures, lighting inconsistencies, background blur, and digital watermark provenance.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP
LESSON 09

Privacy, Copyright & The Future

Where does user data go? How are training sets gathered? Fair use, artist rights, and future career impacts.

Curriculum Objective & Hands-on Deliverable

Overview of copyright lawsuits, open weights vs closed APIs, data retention policies, and human-in-the-loop workforce roles.

High School Grades 09-12 Estimated Time: 25 mins XP Value: 100 XP

Six High-Impact AI Practice Missions

Don't just read about AI. Test it, break it, stress-test it, and fact-check it.

Mission 1: Spot the AI

Sort six everyday technologies into rule-based software, predictive AI, or generative AI.

Deliverable: CREATE → An annotated comparison chart

Mission 2: Stress-test a Model

Train on two types of objects. Change the lighting and background; record where predictions fail.

Deliverable: CREATE → A five-test error log

Mission 3: The Prompt Remix

Compare a vague prompt with a specific one. Change one ingredient and evaluate the difference.

Deliverable: CREATE → Two prompts + a short reflection

Mission 4: Fact-check the Fluent

Check three AI-generated claims using reliable sources. Mark supported, false, or uncertain.

Deliverable: CREATE → A claim-and-source evidence table

Mission 5: Find the Missing Voice

Compare two generated career descriptions. Identify a stereotype and rewrite the prompt fairly.

Deliverable: CREATE → A bias audit + revised prompt

Mission 6: Draw Your AI Boundary

Apply a sample teacher policy to three scenarios. Explain what is allowed and what needs disclosure.

Deliverable: CREATE → A personal responsible-use checklist

High School AI Curriculum Glossary & Knowledge Base

Comprehensive definitions for artificial intelligence literacy and digital mastery.

Artificial Intelligence (AI)
The simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems, specifically the ability to perceive, synthesize, and infer information.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Machine Learning (ML)
A subfield of artificial intelligence focusing on algorithms that improve automatically through experience and the use of data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Deep Learning
A subset of machine learning based on artificial neural networks with representation learning; layers extract progressively higher-level features.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Neural Network
A computational model inspired by biological neural networks in animal brains consisting of connected nodes (artificial neurons).
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Weights and Biases
Learned numerical parameters in a neural network that scale and shift inputs to produce accurate mathematical outputs.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Loss Function
A mathematical function that evaluates how well an AI algorithm models the given dataset; measures the difference between prediction and ground truth.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Gradient Descent
An optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function by iteratively moving in the direction of steepest descent.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Backpropagation
Short for backward propagation of errors, an algorithm used to calculate the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Overfitting
A modeling error in machine learning where a function is too closely aligned to a limited set of data points, performing poorly on new data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Underfitting
Occurs when a machine learning model cannot adequately capture the underlying structure of the data, resulting in poor training and test accuracy.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Large Language Model (LLM)
A specialized deep learning model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand, summarize, generate, and predict human language.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Transformer Architecture
A deep learning neural network model introduced in 2017 utilizing self-attention mechanisms to process sequential data simultaneously.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Self-Attention Mechanism
A mathematical process allowing neural networks to dynamically weigh the importance of different words in a sentence regardless of distance.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Token and Tokenization
The basic building block of text processed by language models; tokens can be words, characters, or subwords (e.g. ~4 characters in English).
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Context Window
The maximum number of tokens an LLM can hold in active memory at once during a conversational interaction or document analysis.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Hallucination
A phenomenon where an LLM generates plausible-sounding statements, citations, or facts that are completely untrue and fabricated.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Grounding
The process of linking model predictions and outputs to verifiable external facts, databases, or authoritative real-world documents.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Prompt Engineering
The discipline of crafting precise instructions, personas, examples, and formatting criteria to guide an AI model to desired outputs.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Few-Shot Prompting
Providing an AI model with a few concrete input-output examples inside the prompt to guide its formatting and style.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Zero-Shot Prompting
Asking an AI model to perform a task directly without giving any preliminary examples.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
A prompting technique that encourages the model to generate intermediate reasoning steps before arriving at a final answer.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Temperature
A hyperparameter in generative models controlling randomness: lower temperature produces deterministic outputs; higher produces creative ones.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Top-P (Nucleus Sampling)
A sampling method that pools only the most probable tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds threshold P.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
A training technique using human evaluations to score model outputs and align AI behavior with human preferences.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Algorithmic Bias
Systematic and repeatable errors in a computer system that create unfair outcomes, such as privileging one arbitrary group over another.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Synthetic Media
Media created or modified using artificial intelligence algorithms, including synthetic images, audio, video, and avatars.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Deepfake
Synthetic media in which a person in an existing image or video is replaced with someone else's likeness using neural networks.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
C2PA Digital Watermarking
Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity cryptographic metadata standard to trace digital content history and origin.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Computer Vision
An interdisciplinary field that deals with how computers can gain high-level understanding from digital images or videos.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
A class of deep neural network commonly applied to analyzing visual imagery through spatial filter kernels.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
A machine learning architecture where two networks (generator and discriminator) compete against each other to produce synthetic data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Diffusion Model
A class of generative latent variable model that generates data by iteratively denoising a random noise tensor into a clear image.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Multimodal AI
Artificial intelligence systems capable of processing and synthesizing multiple types of data simultaneously, such as text, audio, images, and video.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Embeddings
Dense mathematical vector representations of text, images, or audio in high-dimensional space capturing semantic relationships.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Vector Database
A database designed to index, store, and query high-dimensional vector embeddings rapidly using approximate nearest neighbors.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
An AI architecture that searches an external knowledge base for relevant documents and feeds them to an LLM as grounded context.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Agentic Workflow
An architecture where AI models autonomously plan, execute tools, evaluate results, and iterate toward a goal without continuous human prompting.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Alignment
The field of AI safety research focused on steering artificial intelligence systems toward human values, intentions, and ethical boundaries.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Red Teaming
The practice of rigorously probing an AI model for vulnerabilities, security flaws, jailbreaks, toxic outputs, and safety failures.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Jailbreaking
The process of bypassing the safety filters and constraints built into a commercial AI model through adversarial prompting techniques.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI

Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
A machine learning architecture where two networks (generator and discriminator) compete against each other to produce synthetic data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Diffusion Model
A class of generative latent variable model that generates data by iteratively denoising a random noise tensor into a clear image.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Multimodal AI
Artificial intelligence systems capable of processing and synthesizing multiple types of data simultaneously, such as text, audio, images, and video.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Embeddings
Dense mathematical vector representations of text, images, or audio in high-dimensional space capturing semantic relationships.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Vector Database
A database designed to index, store, and query high-dimensional vector embeddings rapidly using approximate nearest neighbors.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
An AI architecture that searches an external knowledge base for relevant documents and feeds them to an LLM as grounded context.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Agentic Workflow
An architecture where AI models autonomously plan, execute tools, evaluate results, and iterate toward a goal without continuous human prompting.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Alignment
The field of AI safety research focused on steering artificial intelligence systems toward human values, intentions, and ethical boundaries.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Red Teaming
The practice of rigorously probing an AI model for vulnerabilities, security flaws, jailbreaks, toxic outputs, and safety failures.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Jailbreaking
The process of bypassing the safety filters and constraints built into a commercial AI model through adversarial prompting techniques.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
The simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems, specifically the ability to perceive, synthesize, and infer information.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Machine Learning (ML)
A subfield of artificial intelligence focusing on algorithms that improve automatically through experience and the use of data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Deep Learning
A subset of machine learning based on artificial neural networks with representation learning; layers extract progressively higher-level features.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Neural Network
A computational model inspired by biological neural networks in animal brains consisting of connected nodes (artificial neurons).
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Weights and Biases
Learned numerical parameters in a neural network that scale and shift inputs to produce accurate mathematical outputs.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Loss Function
A mathematical function that evaluates how well an AI algorithm models the given dataset; measures the difference between prediction and ground truth.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Gradient Descent
An optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function by iteratively moving in the direction of steepest descent.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Backpropagation
Short for backward propagation of errors, an algorithm used to calculate the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Overfitting
A modeling error in machine learning where a function is too closely aligned to a limited set of data points, performing poorly on new data.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Underfitting
Occurs when a machine learning model cannot adequately capture the underlying structure of the data, resulting in poor training and test accuracy.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Large Language Model (LLM)
A specialized deep learning model trained on vast amounts of text data to understand, summarize, generate, and predict human language.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Transformer Architecture
A deep learning neural network model introduced in 2017 utilizing self-attention mechanisms to process sequential data simultaneously.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Self-Attention Mechanism
A mathematical process allowing neural networks to dynamically weigh the importance of different words in a sentence regardless of distance.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Token and Tokenization
The basic building block of text processed by language models; tokens can be words, characters, or subwords (e.g. ~4 characters in English).
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Context Window
The maximum number of tokens an LLM can hold in active memory at once during a conversational interaction or document analysis.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Hallucination
A phenomenon where an LLM generates plausible-sounding statements, citations, or facts that are completely untrue and fabricated.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Grounding
The process of linking model predictions and outputs to verifiable external facts, databases, or authoritative real-world documents.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Prompt Engineering
The discipline of crafting precise instructions, personas, examples, and formatting criteria to guide an AI model to desired outputs.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Few-Shot Prompting
Providing an AI model with a few concrete input-output examples inside the prompt to guide its formatting and style.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Zero-Shot Prompting
Asking an AI model to perform a task directly without giving any preliminary examples.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
A prompting technique that encourages the model to generate intermediate reasoning steps before arriving at a final answer.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Temperature
A hyperparameter in generative models controlling randomness: lower temperature produces deterministic outputs; higher produces creative ones.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Top-P (Nucleus Sampling)
A sampling method that pools only the most probable tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds threshold P.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
A training technique using human evaluations to score model outputs and align AI behavior with human preferences.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Algorithmic Bias
Systematic and repeatable errors in a computer system that create unfair outcomes, such as privileging one arbitrary group over another.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Synthetic Media
Media created or modified using artificial intelligence algorithms, including synthetic images, audio, video, and avatars.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Deepfake
Synthetic media in which a person in an existing image or video is replaced with someone else's likeness using neural networks.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
C2PA Digital Watermarking
Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity cryptographic metadata standard to trace digital content history and origin.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Computer Vision
An interdisciplinary field that deals with how computers can gain high-level understanding from digital images or videos.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
A class of deep neural network commonly applied to analyzing visual imagery through spatial filter kernels.
Category: AI Academy Core Standard: CSTA K-12 AI
Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
A machine learning architecture where two networks (generator and discriminator) compete against each other to produce synthetic data.

A class of generative latent variable model that generates data by iteratively denoising a random noise tensor into a clear image.

Artificial intelligence systems capable of processing and synthesizing multiple types of data simultaneously, such as text, audio, images, and video.
